# `coordtrans()` {#fn-coordtrans}

For a partial photograph the stored positive bearing density must lie within its photographed sector. H07 verified agreement with a complete skyline on the covered north-crossing cases and rejection of uncovered densities. [H07 results](h07-panorama-coverage.qmd).

In D02, declination quantiles agreed with direct propagation within 0.008 degrees across nine terrain and observer cases. Near the celestial pole the discrepancy reached 0.17 degrees on the fine grid; at the pole a zero conditional width prevented calculation. [D02 results](d02-bearing-propagation.qmd).

The integration uses the full bearing density from any of the six measurement families. [Measurement families](orientation-densities.qmd#measurement-families).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-coordtrans)

```{=html}
<p>A sightline has a distribution of possible bearings, and each bearing samples a
potentially different part of the horizon. For every sampled bearing the function
interpolates horizon altitude and uncertainty, maps an altitude range to declination and
approximates the conditional declination distribution by a Gaussian. It weights that
distribution by the azimuth density and integrates the product by the trapezoidal rule.
A shared horizon can serve several observations, or a supplied list can represent their
individual sites.
</p>
<p>Density values are calculated at declination spacing <code>.res</code>, then
linearly interpolated onto a grid with spacing <code>.output.res</code>. The upper
calculation bound is evaluated explicitly if the step does not land on it,
avoiding extrapolation at the tail. Linear interpolation preserves
nonnegative calculated densities and avoids cubic-spline overshoot.
Individual PDF outputs retain their existing area normalisation; SPD outputs
retain their existing unnormalised transformation behaviour. Coarse
calculation spacing can still miss narrow peaks; interpolation does not
replace a resolution-convergence check. Azimuth integration uses a separate
grid from -90 to 450 degrees with step <code>.prec</code>. For a distribution split across north, integration uses contiguous bearings around zero at the same spacing. The output grid starts
at the lower bound and ends at the last full step within the upper bound.
Refine the calculation grid to check that narrow features are resolved.
Set atmospheric refraction, pressure and temperature with <code>skyscapeR.vars</code> before transforming. The values used are recorded in the returned PDF or SPD.
All three spacings are stored in <code>metadata$param</code>.
</p>
```

<details><summary>Method references</summary>

```{=html}
<p>Silva, F (2020) A probabilistic framework and significance test for the analysis of structural orientations
in skyscape archaeology <em>Journal of Archaeological Science</em> 118, 105138. \Sexpr[results=rd]{tools:::Rd_expr_doi("10.1016/j.jas.2020.105138")}
</p>



```

</details>

**Interpretation and limits.** A transformed density inherits the latitude and skyline for its own bearing. Replacing it with a symmetric curve can erase an asymmetric or multimodal distribution created by the terrain.


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>pdf</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>A <em>skyscapeR.pdf</em> object created with <code>az.pdf</code> or a <em>skyscapeR.spd</em> object created with <code>spd</code></p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>hor</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>A shared <code>skyscapeR.horizon</code> or, for individual azimuth PDFs, a list of horizons in measurement order.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>xrange</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Array of values (min and max) for SPD when transforming a <em>skyscapeR.spd</em> object.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>.res</code></th><td><code>0.1</code></td><td><p>Spacing of the declination calculation grid, in degrees. Default 0.1.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>.prec</code></th><td><code>0.1</code></td><td><p>Azimuth integration spacing, in degrees. Default 0.1.
Previously ignored; smaller values increase integration work. Must not exceed 540.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>.output.res</code></th><td><code>0.01</code></td><td><p>Spacing of the returned declination grid, in degrees.
Default 0.01. Coarser spacing reduces output size. All spacings must be
positive finite scalars, and the returned grid must contain at least two points.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>verbose</code></th><td><code>TRUE</code></td><td><p>Logical. Display progress or informational messages. Default <code>TRUE</code>.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>A <code>skyscapeR.pdf</code> object for PDF input, or a <code>skyscapeR.spd</code>
object for SPD input. Both contain <code>metadata</code> and <code>data</code>. PDF data
are a list of data frames with declination <code>x</code> and density <code>y</code>;
SPD data are a single such data frame. Metadata include the coordinate type,
transformation settings, format version and descriptive source labels.
</p>
```
